Scientists can see what cells are made of and observe what they do. But how all those parts come together to create something alive remains one of biology’s biggest mysteries.

On this week’s episode of Unexplainable, University of Minnesota synthetic biologist Kate Adamala explains what we could learn by building cells from scratch.

author: Vox
description:
Are we truly alone in the universe? Despite the lack of hard evidence, belief in aliens and UFOs, officially known as Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP), has shifted from the fringes to the center of mainstream culture.

Subscribe to our channel! http://goo.gl/0bsAjO

In this episode of The Gray Area, host Jonquilyn Hill is joined by Adam Kirsch, senior editor at The Atlantic and author of the new book We Want to Believe: How Aliens Went Mainstream and Why It Matters.

They explore why our fascination with extraterrestrial life persists and what that need to believe tells us about our current relationship with authority, scientific expertise, and even spirituality. The search for aliens has become the ultimate self-portrait of humanity.
